title: X Feed Digest
summary: AI Leadership Shakeups: Major departures at xAI (Jimmy Ba) and Anthropic (safety lead Mrinank Sharma), with cryptic warnings about 2026 being a "consequential" year.
Coding Agent Revolution: OpenAI's Codex hits 1M downloads; developers porting legacy code (SimCity) in days using AI; shifts toward "orchestrator" roles.
Crypto History & Markets: Resurfacing of the legendary 50k BTC OKX liquidation story; discussions on asset ownership vs. labor in the AI era.

items.title: @sama: Codex Growth
items.body: OpenAI's Codex App hit 1M+ downloads in its first week. Sam confirms a free tier will remain available to let everyone try building.

items.title: @jimmybajimmyba: Leaving xAI
items.body: Co-founder Jimmy Ba leaves xAI, predicting "recursive self-improvement loops" within 12 months and calling 2026 the most consequential year for humanity.

items.title: @alex_prompter: Anthropic Safety Exit
items.body: Anthropic's safety lead Mrinank Sharma resigns to study poetry, warning that the world is in peril and criticizing the difficulty of letting values govern actions.

items.title: @ccccjjjjeeee: SimCity Port
items.body: A developer used Codex to port the original 1989 SimCity C codebase to TypeScript/browser in just a few days with minimal manual intervention.

items.title: @obsdmd: Obsidian CLI
items.body: Obsidian releases an official CLI, unlocking powerful automation potential for AI agents to manage notes and vaults directly.

items.title: @Bqlsj2023: The 50k BTC Liquidation
items.body: A retrospective on the massive 2018 OKX liquidation event where a user ('50k Sister') went long with 50,000 BTC, causing a massive market impact and exchange intervention.

items.title: @AviFelman: Ownership vs Labor
items.body: Argues that in an era of AI deflation and monetary inflation, the true divide will be between those who own the 'machine' (assets) and those who just use it.

items.title: @ExpLang_Cn: First Principles Thinking
items.body: A deep dive into First Principles Thinking vs. Analogy Thinking, using SpaceX and Airbnb as examples for breaking down problems to basic truths.

items.title: @neogoose_btw: Code Quality
items.body: Humorous comparison: Apollo 11 had 40k lines of code, while modern 'slop' pull requests are bloated messes.
